interactions.summary: Jiang explains that Dante could be bold because the Church was internally split, then resumes the close reading by contrasting Paul's faith as obedience to unseen truth with Dante's faith as imagination that helps make truth real.
A student reads the passage where Peter examines Dante's faith by asking whether the coin of faith has been properly tested and whether Dante carries it in his purse.

Jiang asks why faith is figured as a coin, a student links the image to indulgences, Jiang rejects indulgences as evil, and the student extends the idea by suggesting that coin-language evokes paying one's way into belief or righteousness.

claims.claim: Jiang says Dante could push his critique because the Catholic Church was split between rival centers and rival papal factions, leaving no single authority able to suppress him cleanly.
He restates Paul's formulation of faith as evidence of things unseen and says science can never prove God's existence.

Jiang contrasts Paul with Dante by saying Paul treats faith as humility and obedience toward realities beyond imagination, whereas Dante treats faith as an act of imagination that proactively helps bring reality into being.
The exchange around the coin image keeps indulgences in view as a possible background for why monetary language around faith is spiritually dangerous.

signature_moments.moment: Faith ceases to be mere obedience and becomes an imaginative act that helps make what it believes in true.
signature_moments.source_phrase: Faith is an act of imagination
signature_moments.why_it_matters: This is one of Jiang's core reversals of standard Christian language and directly extends his earlier claim that 'we are the plan.'

signature_moments.moment: Peter's exam turns faith into a coin whose alloy, weight, and placement in the purse can be tested.
signature_moments.why_it_matters: The image launches Jiang's inquiry into why a spiritual virtue is being described in the language of money and exchange.

glossary_terms.definition_or_usage: The image Jiang pauses over in Canto 24, where faith is examined like currency for purity, weight, and whether it is truly possessed.

chronology_notes.note: Jiang briefly historicizes Dante's boldness through the late-medieval split Church before turning back to the immediate close reading of Canto 24.

uncertainty_notes.note: ASR distorts place names in Jiang's quick account of the rival papal centers, so preserve the broader split-Church explanation without overfitting the malformed proper nouns.
